name: PersistedQueryRegistry
purpose: SHA-256 -> query allow-list that lets production clients send deterministic 64-char ids instead of raw queries; unregistered ids are rejected.

invariants.rule: Hash id is lowercase sha-256 hex of UTF-8 query bytes; registration is idempotent.
get() never returns a query whose re-hash differs from the id (tamper detection).
Registry is read-only in production mode; register() in prod raises PQRImmutableError.
Lookup is O(1) in the backing store.
Callers cannot enumerate registered ids (no public list() -- privacy).

extension_contract: Adopters pass an optional snapshot_sink invoked after each registration to persist the state (disk, Redis, S3). Hash function is sealed; no weaker hash substitution.
consumption_example:
reg = InMemoryPersistedQueryRegistry()
qid = reg.register('query { me { id } }')
reg.freeze()
assert reg.contains(qid)
why_essential: Without a persisted-query gate, production GraphQL or parametric-SQL endpoints accept arbitrary queries from clients; the surface enables resource exhaustion attacks and leaks internal schema shape.
alternatives_considered: Server-side exact-string allow-list: leaks through whitespace differences.
Signed-query JWT: solves integrity but not allow-listing.
Disabling introspection only: closes discovery, not arbitrary queries.
